title: CDI – Interpretation of Lab Results
summary: CDI is a toxin mediated disease. Not all patients with Clostridium difficile have toxin detected in their stool samples, therefore the testing process for Clostridium difficile is now a two/three stage test to increase sensitivity of detection. GDH test: detects antigen of both toxigenic and non-toxigenic C. difficile. PCR test: detects presence of toxin gene. Toxin test: detects presence of toxin.
changeSummary: Initial transcription from Eolas Medical, Northern Ireland Primary Care Antimicrobial Guidelines (v5.119.0).
clinicalNotes: GDH positive and/or PCR positive, and toxin positive (PPV 91.4%): C. difficile infection most likely to be present and may require treatment.

GDH positive and/or PCR positive, and toxin negative: C. difficile could be present (confirmed present if PCR positive). Potential for C. difficile excretion and transmission. Clinical assessment required to diagnose infection and treatment.
GDH negative and toxin negative (NPV 98.9%): C. difficile infection very unlikely. Patient could have other potential pathogens.

regimens.label: Interpretation only – no antibiotic regimen in this section
notes: For treatment, see CDI – Diagnosis and Treatment Options.
